einzeiler: 律所代表9岁女孩起诉社交媒体公司
kurzfassung: 律所代表因过度使用社交媒体而受到伤害的9岁女孩Kaylee提起诉讼。律师Mark Lanier与Meta和YouTube等科技巨头在法庭上展开对抗。最终陪审团裁定这些公司对儿童造成了伤害。
stichpunkte: 律师Mark Lanier及其女儿接手了一起代表9岁女孩Kaylee的案件
Kaylee因过度沉迷YouTube和Instagram而身心受创
Meta和YouTube被指控故意设计让用户上瘾的功能
Mark Lanier利用人工智能模拟陪审员来排练辩论
Mark Zuckerberg等Meta团队出庭应诉并引发争议
陪审团最终裁定这些科技公司对女孩造成的伤害负有责任

今天用B1级别英语讲述的真实故事，是关于一位律师走进法庭，对抗最强大的公司，为孩子们抵御社交媒体的故事。
Today's true story in B1 English is of a lawyer going into court against the most powerful companies to defend children against social media.

这是大卫对抗歌利亚。
This is David versus Goliath.

Mark Lanier的女儿带着一个新案子来找他。
Mark Lanier's daughter came to him with a new case.

“爸爸，加州有一个女孩需要你。”
"Daddy, there's a girl who needs you in California."

Mark是一名律师，而且Mark已经打败过一些最大的公司。他是一个65岁的男人，有12个孙辈。
Mark was a lawyer, and Mark had already beaten some of the biggest companies. He was a 65-year-old man with 12 grandkids.

如今他的女儿Rachel，也是一名律师，已经为一个新案子准备了好几个月。她有证据，她有证人。
Now his daughter Rachel, also a lawyer, was building a new case for many months. She had evidence, she had witnesses.

现在她的父亲可以把这个案子带上法庭了。
Now her father could take it into the courtroom.

�
这个案子是关于一个9岁的女孩，Kaylee。
This case was about a 9-year-old girl, Kaylee.

Kaylee在6岁的时候就迷上了YouTube。她9岁的时候就在用Instagram了。
Now, Kaylee got hooked on YouTube when she was 6 years old. She was on Instagram when she was 9.

到了10岁，Kaylee就不出自己的卧室了。Kaylee在学校里成绩不及格，她甚至开始割伤自己、伤害自己。
By 10 years old, Kaylee wasn't leaving her bedroom. Kaylee was failing at school, and she was even cutting and hurting herself.

每一次她妈妈把手机拿走，这个女孩都会控制不住地发抖和哭泣。
Every time her mother took the phone away, the girl shook and cried uncontrollably.

有一天，Kaylee在Instagram上花了超过16个小时。一天之内16个小时。
One day, Kaylee spent more than 16 hours on Instagram. 16 hours in one day.

在洛杉矶法庭的一边，是Mark Lanier和他的女儿们。
On one side of the Los Angeles courtroom is Mark Lanier and his daughters.

在法庭的另一边，是世界上最强大的两家公司，Meta和YouTube，还有几十位世界上最顶尖的律师，以及Mark Zuckerberg本人——Meta的首席执行官，他拥有Facebook和Instagram。
On the other side of the courtroom is two of the world's most powerful companies, Meta and YouTube, and dozens of the world's best lawyers, and Mark Zuckerberg himself, the CEO of Meta, who owns Facebook and Instagram.

对Mark Lanier来说，这是一场圣战——一场争夺我们孩子心灵的战争。
For Mark Lanier, this is a holy war — the war for the minds of our children.

在这场审判中，Mark Zuckerberg和他的团队走进了法庭，而他们全都戴着内置隐藏摄像头的Meta眼镜。
In this trial, Mark Zuckerberg walked into the courtroom with his team, and they were all wearing Meta glasses with hidden cameras inside.

Mark Lanier在德克萨斯州长大，童年很普通。他的父亲是一名销售员，母亲是一名家庭主妇。
Mark Lanier grew up in Texas, an ordinary childhood. His father was a salesman and his mother a housewife.

Mark上的是美国最便宜的法学院之一。学费每小时只要4美元。
Mark went to one of the cheapest law schools in America. It cost only $4 per hour.

Mark是一个很有天赋的演讲者。当他说话的时候，他说得很有力量，人们都会听他说。在他做律师的头五年里，他赢下了每一个案子。
Mark was a talented speaker. When he spoke, he spoke with power, and people listened to him. In his first five years as a lawyer, he won every case.

然而，他还是输了一次。而且他本来就应该输，他活该输。
Still, he lost. And he should have lost, and he deserved to lose.

他为一家他明知有罪的公司辩护。
He fought for a company who he knew was guilty.

“我到底在做什么？”
"What am I doing?"

Mark在开车回家的路上这样问自己。他输掉的这个案子——嗯，它改变了他的人生。
Mark asked himself as he drove home. This case he'd lost — well, it changed his life.

于是Mark开办了自己的律师事务所。这样他就可以选择接哪些案子，他就可以只选择那些他自己相信的案子。Mark说：“你可以用这种力量做可怕的事，但你也可以用它做伟大的事。”
So Mark started his own law firm. This way he could choose which cases to take, and he could choose only cases that he believed in. Mark says, "You can do horrible things with this power, but you can also do great things."

Mark为普通人，为我，为你，从制药公司、从化工公司那里赢得了将近200亿美元。
Mark won nearly $20 billion for ordinary people, for me, for you, from drug companies, from chemical companies.

但Meta和YouTube，它们是完全不同的猛兽。它们是歌利亚，而Mark是大卫。
But Meta and YouTube, they were a different beast. They were Goliath, and Mark was David.

�
距离开庭还有四个月。
Four months until the trial.

Mark的主要任务是用证据证明，这些应用造成伤害不是出于意外，而是出于设计。
Mark's main task is to prove with evidence that these apps cause harm not by accident, but by design.

是故意造成伤害。
Cause harm on purpose.

Mark Lanier本来可以向法庭索要一大笔钱，但他反而什么都没有要。
Mark Lanier, he could ask the court for a huge sum of money, but instead he asks them for nothing.

Mark是一个有宗教信仰的人。每个星期天他都在当地的教堂教授耶稣的教义，而且Mark还痴迷于人工智能。
Mark is a religious man. Every Sunday he teaches the lessons of Jesus at his local church, and Mark is also obsessed with AI.

所以在法庭上有陪审团。陪审团就是那12个人，12位普通公民，就像你妈妈，就像你爸爸。陪审团的工作就是决定一个人是无罪还是有罪。
So in the court there is the jury. The jury is the 12 people, 12 ordinary citizens, like your mum, like your dad. The jury's job is to decide if someone is innocent or guilty.

于是Mark制作了全部12位陪审员的AI版本。
So Mark made AI versions of all 12 of the jury members.

他知道陪审员的年龄、他们的工作、他们的家庭状况，而且他还知道每一位陪审员最敬佩的三个人和最不敬佩的三个人。
So he knew the jury's age, their job, their family situation, and he knew the three people each jury member admired the most and admired the least.

然后Mark为每一位陪审员的头脑做了一个AI复制品。
And Mark made an AI copy of each of the jury's mind.

Mark每天晚上都在这12个AI版本的陪审员身上练习他的论证。他问他们对这个证人、那个证人怎么看。他问他们那天有什么可能让他们感到困惑。
Mark practiced his arguments on the 12 AI versions of the jury every night. He asked them what they thought of this witness, that witness. He asked what might have confused them that day.

他说，他平均每晚只睡四个小时。“睡眠是一种额外的好处，”他说，“但不是必需品。”
He slept, he says, on average just four hours a night. "Sleep's a bonus," he said, "but not one that's necessary."

�️
开庭审判。
The trial.

审判一开始，Meta就说：“这个女孩的问题来自她艰难的童年。她的问题不是来自Instagram。”
As the trial starts, Meta says, "The girl's problems come from her difficult childhood. Her problems don't come from Instagram."

Mark说：“法庭上的各位。
Mark says, "People of the court.

“仅仅因为一个人本来就头痛，”他说，“这并不给你用石头砸他的权利。”然后再说：“他们本来就头痛。不是我的错。”
Just because someone already has a headache," he said, "that doesn't give you the right to hit them with a rock." And then say, "They already had a headache. Not my fault."

Mark和他的女儿们日夜工作，收集了数百万页的证据，而他们找到了黄金。
Mark and his daughters worked day and night collecting millions of pages of evidence, and they found gold.

YouTube在2012年的一条内部消息说，它的目标不是获得更多的观众。哦不，它的目标是让观众上瘾。
A YouTube message from 2012 said that its goal was not to get more viewers. Oh no, its goal was to make viewers addicted.

另一份文件说：“这些平台是注意力赌场。而庄家永远是赢家。”
Another document said, "These platforms are attention casinos. And the house always wins."

Meta在2018年的一份文件说：“为了让更多青少年使用这个平台，我们必须让更多儿童来使用它。”
A Meta document from 2018 said, "To get more teenagers using the platform, we've got to get more children to use it."

然后Mark Lanier向陪审团展示了这些平台上的安全功能——就是那些安全功能，让父母可以控制他们的孩子看什么、看多久。
Then Mark Lanier showed the jury the safety features on these platforms — so the safety features, so parents can control what their children watch and how long for.

但是这些安全功能非常难找到，而且它们在30天之后会自动关闭。
But these safety features are very hard to find, and they automatically switch themselves off after 30 days.

�️
第二天，Mark Zuckerberg本人走了进来，Meta的首席执行官，带着他所有的安保团队和律师。
The next day, Mark Zuckerberg himself walks in, the CEO of Meta, with all his security team and lawyers.

Zuckerberg和他团队里的每一个人，全都戴着Meta的新款智能眼镜。
Zuckerberg and every one of his team, all wearing Meta's new smart glasses.

人们笑了，但是Mark Lanier，他没有笑。这本应是一个保密的陪审团，意思是这12个人不该被任何人辨认出来。而现在Mark Zuckerberg和他那价值十亿美元的团队走了进来，戴着那些鬼鬼祟祟的新眼镜，里面全都装着摄像头。
People laugh, but Mark Lanier, he does not laugh. This was supposed to be a secret jury, meaning the jury should be 12 people nobody can identify. And now Mark Zuckerberg and his billion dollar team walk in with those sneaky new glasses that all have cameras inside them.

（相机音效）
(Camera sound effect)

“把你们的眼镜摘下来。”法官说。
"Take off your glasses," says the judge.

Zuckerberg和他的团队一个接一个地摘下他们的Meta眼镜，并发誓他们没有已经拍下陪审团的照片。
One by one, Zuckerberg and his team take off their Meta glasses and swear they didn't already take photographs of the jury.

也许这是这些人第一次被人说“不”。
And maybe it was the first time these boys were told "no."

�️
Mark Zuckerberg出庭作证。
Mark Zuckerberg takes the stand.

这是Meta首席执行官Mark Zuckerberg第一次必须在法庭上向陪审团作出回答。
This is the first time Mark Zuckerberg, the CEO of Meta, has to answer to a jury in a court.

Mark Lanier向在场的人展示，美国所有11岁孩子中有三分之一在使用Instagram。
Mark Lanier shows the room how one-third of all 11-year-olds in America uses Instagram.

但是怎么会呢？13岁以下的孩子是不被允许拥有账号的。
But how? Under-13s aren't allowed accounts.

然后Mark Lanier向在场的人展示了一幅巨大的拼贴画，也就是许多照片粘贴在一起。
Then Mark Lanier shows the room a giant collage, which is many photographs all stuck together.

一份15米宽的巨大文件，上面有数百张照片和自拍，全都是一个女孩发布的——Kaylee，用滤镜改变着她的脸。
A huge document 15 meters wide, hundreds of photos and selfies all posted by one girl — Kaylee, with filters changing her face.

然后Mark向这位世界上最富有的人之一问了一个简单的问题。
And Mark asks one of the richest men in the world a simple question.

“Zuckerberg先生，Meta有没有看过这个女孩的账号，并为她担心过？”
"Mr. Zuckerberg, has Meta ever looked at this girl's account and worried about her?"

Mark Zuckerberg什么都没说。
Mark Zuckerberg doesn't say anything.

一个合理的问题。
A fair question.

Meta有没有为这个女孩担心过？
Has Meta ever worried about this girl?

一片沉默。
Silence.

�
七周之后，审判结束了，陪审团走进了后面的房间。
After seven weeks, the trial finishes and the jury go into the back room.

是时候做决定了。
Time to decide.

Meta和YouTube是否犯了伤害儿童的罪？
Is Meta and YouTube guilty of harming children?

他们等了一天，三天，八天。陪审团一直待在那个房间里讨论、决定。
They wait one day, three days, eight days. The jury stays inside that room talking, deciding.

2026年3月25日，陪审团，这12位普通人，走了出来，给出了他们的答案。
On March 25, 2026, the jury, 12 ordinary people, come back out and give their answer.

这些公司对这个女孩造成了伤害，而且他们早就知道，他们还是照做了。
These companies caused harm to the girl, and they had known, and they had done it anyways.

Mark Lanier说，可悲的事实是，政客永远不会阻止这些公司。他说，这些公司真正害怕的唯一一群人，就是陪审团里那12个普通人。
Mark Lanier says the sad truth is, politicians will never stop these companies. The only people these companies are truly afraid of, he says, are the 12 ordinary people in the jury.

陪审员并不会从中得到金钱、名声或权力。
The jury do not get money, reputation or power from this.

他们唯一的工作，就是手按胸口说出真相。
Their only job is to tell the truth with one hand on their heart.

而那，我的朋友们，就是法治制度的力量，在这种制度下，连最富有的人和国王都必须对法律作出回答。
And that, my friends, is the power of the rule of law system, when even the richest people and kings must answer to the law.

拥有法治制度的国家意味着法律是最高的权力，连总统都必须对它作出回答。
Countries with a rule of law system means that the law is the highest power, and even the president must answer to it.

而且，容我说一句，这个法治制度顺便说是起源于英格兰的，大约在800年前，当时的国王约翰不得不签署一份文件来阻止一场内战。但直到今天，《大宪章》，也就是他那份原始的文件，依然是许许多多国家法治制度的基础。
And, may I say, this rule of law system started in England, by the way, about 800 years ago, when King John had to sign a document to stop a civil war. But still today, the Magna Carta, which is his original document, this is the foundation for the rule of law system in so many countries.

但即使在今天，仍然有非常多的国家，在那里一个九岁的女孩永远、永远不可能有机会战胜这样的金钱和权力。
But still today, there are so many countries where a nine year old girl would never, never have a chance of winning against this kind of money and power.

So why is this so important?
